candidate.title: Aba-seq
candidate.scope: The middle row headed Aba-seq in the supplied Illumina poster crop: the bulk genomic DNA workflow from native 5hmC through glucosylation, AbaSI cleavage, biotinylated-adaptor ligation, fragmentation and affinity-selected DNA. AbaSI coupled with sequencing is the expanded name, not another target. JBP1-seq and TAmC-Seq are separately labeled neighboring catalogue rows, not alternatives of this assigned Aba-seq workflow; the clipped upper T-WGBS row is also outside scope. The verified collection page is headed Aba-seq and reproduces this route; its discussions of scAba-seq, PvuRts1I and SCL-exo do not expand the target. The Sun et al. 2013 implementation clarifies the adaptor and readout interface without expanding unshown library completion into operations.

operations.label: AbaSI
operations.description: Cleave the glucosylated DNA near recognized modified cytosines, changing continuous duplexes into fragments with characteristic cleavage boundaries.
operations.mechanism: AbaSI creates double-stranded breaks at a narrow range of distances from 5gmC; recognition is modification dependent. The primary paper reports no digestion of 5mC or C under its tested conditions; this is not a universal claim about all substrates or conditions.
operations.information_effect: The new DNA ends carry positional information about nearby original 5hmC. They do not directly read the modification. Cleavage efficiency depends on the local recognition context.

operations.label: Fragment
operations.description: Break adaptor-ligated DNA into shorter pieces, retaining tagged terminal fragments alongside untagged internal DNA.
operations.mechanism: The poster labels the operation broadly as fragmentation; the primary implementation uses sonication.
operations.information_effect: The cleavage boundary stays associated with its tagged terminal genomic fragment. Secondary fragment ends are not additional 5hmC recognition events.

operations.label: Streptavidin magnetic bead pull down
operations.description: Bind and retain fragments carrying biotinylated terminal adaptors on streptavidin magnetic beads; untagged internal fragments are not the selected product. The drawing then summarizes this selected material as DNA.
operations.mechanism: Streptavidin–biotin affinity captures the biotin on the ligated DNA adaptor, rather than binding native 5hmC directly.
operations.information_effect: The measured carrier is genomic DNA adjacent to adaptor-tagged AbaSI cleavage boundaries. In the primary implementation, reads begin at P1b and are mapped to locate the cuts; nearby candidate original 5hmC sites are inferred using the expected cleavage offsets and reference cytosines. The modification is represented by a cleavage-position association rather than by a direct modified-base read. Context-dependent cleavage efficiency limits representation, and multiple candidate cytosines can make exact-base assignment ambiguous (13% of identified cleavage sites in the reported E14 dataset). Capture selects the biotinylated adaptor, so capture alone does not independently verify the biological specificity of every selected fragment.

method_scopes.rationale: All five local operations belong to the single Aba-seq row, linked by arrows. The left target icon is descriptive; biotinylated oligos are a reagent input. The fragmentation output contains tagged and untagged pieces, followed by selective capture, rather than an alternative assay branch. This schematic matches the glucosylation/AbaSI/P1b/fragmentation/capture architecture described in the primary Aba-seq paper; it makes no claim that other 5hmC assays or the unshown single-cell variation share every interface.
